1	defmodule Dockd.Instance do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  A view of a Docker container that dockd manages.
4	
5	  An `Instance` is derived state: it is hydrated on demand from the Docker
6	  daemon (via `find_container/2` or `list_containers/2`) and is never
7	  long-lived. After a dockd process crashes or restarts, the world still
8	  looks the same — every `Dockd.apply/2`-created container carries the
9	  marker label `org.dockd.instance=true` and the instance name as
10	  `org.dockd.instance.name`, so `Dockd.list/1` can rebuild the full set of
11	  instances by querying Docker alone.
12	
13	  The struct is intentionally minimal: it carries identity, the parts of
14	  the container's runtime configuration that callers commonly need, and a

3	  Public API for dockd.
4	
5	  Dockd manages local Docker containers as named instances ("instances"). The
6	  API is intentionally stateless: there is no in-process registry, no GenServer,
7	  no local store. Every container that dockd creates carries the marker label
8	  `org.dockd.instance=true` plus its instance name as
9	  `org.dockd.instance.name`, so a fresh BEAM can rediscover the full set of
10	  managed instances by querying Docker alone.
11	
12	  ## Getting Started
13	
14	  With a Docker daemon running locally, apply an installed package by name and
15	  you have a live instance:
16	
17	      > {:ok, %Dockd.ApplyResult{instance: instance}} = Dockd.apply_package("webapp")
18	
19	  ### One-shot commands
20	
21	  `shell_command/3` runs a single command and returns its output and
22	  exit code. Each call is independent — no shell state carries over
23	  between calls.
24	
25	      > {:ok, %{output: _, running: false, exit_code: 0}} =
26	      ...>   Dockd.shell_command(instance, ["echo", "hello"])
27	
28	      # Fresh exec each time — `cd` in one call does not affect the next.
29	      > {:ok, %{exit_code: 0}} = Dockd.shell_command(instance, "cd /tmp")
30	      > {:ok, %{output: "/\\n"}} = Dockd.shell_command(instance, "pwd")

35	  variables, an authenticated session), open a single shell with
36	  `open_shell/2` and thread the handle through `shell_send/3`. Close

50	  provisioning pipeline (pull or build, create, start, fetch repos,
51	  copy files, run setup steps). The returned `Dockd.Instance` is a
52	  view of the live container — pass it (or its name) to any other
53	  function in this module. See "Packages" below for the full
54	  resolution rules and how to install additional package sets from
55	  git.
56	
57	  ## Lifecycle
58	
59	    - `apply/2` — create a container from a `Dockd.Spec`. Returns a
60	      `Dockd.ApplyResult` carrying the resulting `Dockd.Instance` and any
61	      step results from provisioning.
62	    - `apply_package/2` — same as `apply/2` but loads the `Spec` from a
63	      JSON package file (see "Packages" below).
64	    - `list/1` — enumerate every dockd-managed `Instance` currently on the
65	      daemon.
66	    - `get/2` — fetch one `Instance` by its instance name.
67	    - `start/2` / `stop/2` / `restart/2` — control the container without
68	      destroying it.
69	    - `destroy/2` — stop and remove an instance.
70	
71	  ## Packages
72	
73	  A package is a directory under the configured packages root containing a
74	  `package.json` (the serialized `Dockd.Spec`: image, shell, env,
75	  mounts, repos, copies, setup steps, etc.) plus any supporting files
76	  the spec references — typically a `Dockerfile` for `build`-based
77	  packages. The directory name is the package's identity.
78	
79	  `apply_package/2` resolves its reference the same way the `mix dockd`
80	  CLI does:
81	
82	    - any string ending in `.json` is treated as a literal file path
83	    - any other string containing `/` is treated as a package directory
84	      and resolves to `<dir>/package.json`
85	    - any other string is resolved against
86	      `<packages_root>/<name>/package.json`
87	
88	  Packages generated or installed into the package root can be applied by
89	  basename:
90	
91	      # Resolves to <packages_root>/webapp/package.json
92	      {:ok, %Dockd.ApplyResult{instance: instance}} =
93	        Dockd.apply_package("webapp")
94	
95	      # Same, with per-call Docker options.
96	      {:ok, result} =
97	        Dockd.apply_package("webapp", socket: "/var/run/docker.sock")
98	
99	      # Explicit directory.
100	      {:ok, result} = Dockd.apply_package("./my-stack")
101	
102	      # Explicit file path.
103	      {:ok, result} = Dockd.apply_package("./my-stack/package.json")
104	
105	  Additional packages can be fetched from a git repository with
106	  `install_packages/2` (or `mix dockd.package.install --source git --git-url=<url>`).
107	  Every `<repo>/packages/<name>/` directory that contains a `package.json` is
108	  copied into `<packages_root>/<name>/`, after which the package can be applied
109	  by name.
110	
111	  ## Visibility
112	
113	    - `running?/2` — boolean liveness check.
114	    - `logs/2` — fetch container stdout/stderr as a binary.
115	    - `inspect/2` — return the raw Docker inspect map (escape hatch for
116	      ports, networks, exit code, started_at, etc.).
117	    - `refresh/2` — re-fetch a fresh `Instance` from Docker after a state
118	      change.
119	
120	  ## Operating on instances
121	
122	    - `shell_command/3` — one-shot exec, captures stdout/stderr and exit
123	      code.
124	    - `open_shell/2` / `shell_send/3` / `close_shell/1` — persistent
125	      interactive shell, state preserved between commands.
126	    - `copy_to/3` — upload host files into an existing instance.
127	
128	  ## Host-side staging
129	
130	  Dockd writes copied files and cloned repos to a staging dir under
131	  `<system_tmp>/dockd/` before uploading them into containers. These
132	  functions report and clean up that local staging dir:
133	
134	    - `list_temp_files/1`
135	    - `delete_temp_files/1`
136	
137	  And the broader, extension-friendly aggregate:
138	
139	    - `info/1` — returns `%{temp_files: %{...}}` today, more keys later.
140	
141	  All public functions accept a per-call `opts` keyword list for caller
142	  runtime context: `:socket`, `:host`, `:api_version`, `:platform`,
143	  `:networks`, `:network_mode`, and the policy flag `:disk_mount_enabled`.
144	  None of these survive on the container.
145	
146	  All implementation lives in `Dockd.Core`; the functions in this module
147	  are thin forwarders.
148	  """

158	
159	  Three input shapes are accepted:
160	
161	    - a `%Dockd.Spec{}` — used as-is
162	    - an image string plus a keyword list of spec options (the Elixir-native
163	      shape; equivalent to calling `Dockd.Spec.from_opts/2` first)
164	    - an image string alone — equivalent to `Spec.from_opts(image, [])`
165	
166	  Per-call options (Docker connection settings and `:disk_mount_enabled`)
167	  and spec options share the same flat keyword list as the second
168	  argument. `Dockd.Spec.option_keys/0` decides the split: any key it
169	  claims is routed into `Spec.from_opts/2`, anything else is treated as
170	  a per-call option. Unknown keys are rejected.
171	
172	  ## Examples
173	
174	      # Image string alone — generates a container name automatically.
175	      {:ok, %Dockd.ApplyResult{instance: instance}} =
176	        Dockd.apply("busybox:1.37.0")
177	
178	      # Image plus spec options.
179	      {:ok, %Dockd.ApplyResult{instance: instance}} =
180	        Dockd.apply("busybox:1.37.0",
181	          name: "smoke",
182	          shell: "/bin/sh",
183	          env: ["FOO=bar"],
184	          steps: [%{run: "mkdir -p /work"}]
185	        )
186	
187	      # Spec options and per-call options share one flat keyword list.
188	      {:ok, result} =
189	        Dockd.apply("busybox:1.37.0",
190	          name: "smoke",
191	          shell: "/bin/sh",
192	          socket: "/var/run/docker.sock"

197	      {:ok, result} = Dockd.apply(spec, socket: "/var/run/docker.sock")
198	
199	      # Failure path: the error may carry the partially-created instance so
200	      # the caller can clean up.
201	      case Dockd.apply("busybox:1.37.0", steps: [%{run: "exit 1"}]) do
202	        {:ok, %Dockd.ApplyResult{instance: instance}} ->
203	          instance
204	
205	        {:error, %Dockd.Error{instance: instance}} when not is_nil(instance) ->
206	          Dockd.destroy(instance)
207	      end

210	          {:ok, ApplyResult.t()} | {:error, Error.t()}

213	  end

@doc """
  Returns a deterministic content fingerprint for a spec.

  The fingerprint is a lowercase SHA-256 hex digest over the spec's declarative
  fields (image, shell, build, steps, repos, copies, env, mounts, labels, name,
  description). It is stable across processes and runs: map keys are sorted
  recursively before hashing, so two specs with the same content — regardless of
  key insertion order — produce the same digest.

  `Dockd.up/2` stamps this digest onto the container as a label at create time
  and recomputes it on a later `up` to decide whether the package spec has
  drifted (destroy + re-provision) or is unchanged (just start).
  """
  @spec fingerprint(t()) :: binary()
  def fingerprint(%__MODULE__{} = spec) do
    digest =
      spec
      |> Map.from_struct()
      |> canonical()
      |> :erlang.term_to_binary()

    :sha256
    |> :crypto.hash(digest)
    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  # Recursively rewrite maps into key-sorted lists so the encoding is
  # independent of map insertion order. Lists (including keyword lists and
  # env/mount tuples' option lists) are walked element-wise; everything else —
  # binaries, atoms, integers, tuples — is left as-is.
  defp canonical(map) when is_map(map) do
    map
    |> Enum.map(fn {k, v} -> {to_string(k), canonical(v)} end)
    |> Enum.sort()
  end

  defp canonical(list) when is_list(list), do: Enum.map(list, &canonical/1)
  defp canonical(other), do: other

  @doc """
  Prefixes a instance name with `dockd-` unless it already starts with that
  prefix.
  """

defmodule DockdCLI.Commands.Instance.Up do
  @moduledoc """
  Installs a package (if not already installed) and idempotently brings its
  instance up in one command.

  Wraps `Dockd.up/2`. Unlike `instance run`, `up` never waits to tear the
  container down — it ensures the instance is running and returns, leaving it
  in place.

  ## Args

  `args[:package]` — the package reference to bring up (required). Resolved the
    same way `apply_package` resolves names: a bare name against the packages
    root, or a `/`-containing path / `.json` file directly.
  `args[:source]` — a git URL to install the package from when it isn't already
    installed. Ignored when the package is already present.
  `args[:name]` — instance name override (defaults to the package's own name).
  """

  alias Dockd.Instance
  alias DockdCLI.Json
  alias DockdCLI.Output

  @spec run(map(), keyword()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def run(args, opts) do
    with {:ok, ref} <- require_package(args) do
      case Dockd.up(ref, up_opts(args) ++ opts) do
        {:ok, summary} -> report(summary)
        {:error, %Dockd.Error{} = err} -> {:error, Exception.message(err)}
      end
    end
  end

  @spec run_json(map(), keyword()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def run_json(args, opts) do
    with {:ok, ref} <- require_package(args) do
      case Dockd.up(ref, up_opts(args) ++ opts) do
        {:ok, %{package: package, action: action, instance: instance}} ->
          Output.json(Map.merge(Json.instance(instance), %{package: package, action: action}))

        {:error, err} ->
          {:error, err}
      end
    end
  end

  defp require_package(args) do
    case Map.get(args, :package) do
      ref when is_binary(ref) and ref != "" -> {:ok, ref}
      _ -> {:error, "Usage: dockd instance up --package NAME [--source URL] [--name NAME]"}
    end
  end

  defp up_opts(args) do
    []
    |> put_present(:source, args[:source])
    |> put_present(:name, args[:name])
  end

  defp put_present(opts, _key, value) when value in [nil, ""], do: opts
  defp put_present(opts, key, value), do: Keyword.put(opts, key, value)

  defp report(%{package: package, action: action, instance: instance}) do
    name = Instance.short_name(instance)
    if package == :installed, do: Output.info("Installed package.")
    Output.info(action_message(action, name))
    Output.info("\nOpen a shell with:\n\n    dockd instance shell --name #{name}")
    :ok
  end

  defp action_message(:created, name), do: "Created and started #{name}."
  defp action_message(:started, name), do: "Started #{name}."
  defp action_message(:running, name), do: "#{name} is already up to date and running."
  defp action_message(:recreated, name), do: "Package spec changed - recreated #{name}."
end

defmodule Dockd.UpTest do
  # Integration test: requires a running Docker daemon. Exercises the
  # install-if-missing + idempotent-start flow behind `dockd instance up`.
  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

  alias Dockd.Instance

  @image "busybox:1.37.0"

  setup do
    root = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "dockd-up-test-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}")
    File.mkdir_p!(root)
    on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf(root) end)
    {:ok, root: root, opts: [packages_path: root]}
  end

  test "provisions when absent, then is idempotent on the second call", %{root: root, opts: opts} do
    name = unique_name()
    write_package(root, name, @image, env: ["A=1"])
    on_exit(fn -> Dockd.destroy(name, opts) end)

    assert {:ok, %{package: :present, action: :created, instance: %Instance{} = inst}} =
             Dockd.up(name, opts)

    assert inst.running?
    assert {:ok, true} = Dockd.running?(name, opts)

    # Second call: unchanged spec, still running -> no-op.
    assert {:ok, %{action: :running, instance: inst2}} = Dockd.up(name, opts)
    assert inst2.id === inst.id
  end

  test "starts an existing but stopped instance without recreating it", %{root: root, opts: opts} do
    name = unique_name()
    write_package(root, name, @image, env: ["A=1"])
    on_exit(fn -> Dockd.destroy(name, opts) end)

    assert {:ok, %{action: :created, instance: inst}} = Dockd.up(name, opts)
    assert :ok = Dockd.stop(inst, opts)

    assert {:ok, %{action: :started, instance: started}} = Dockd.up(name, opts)
    assert started.id === inst.id
    assert started.running?
  end

  test "recreates the instance when the package spec changes", %{root: root, opts: opts} do
    name = unique_name()
    write_package(root, name, @image, env: ["A=1"])
    on_exit(fn -> Dockd.destroy(name, opts) end)

    assert {:ok, %{action: :created, instance: inst}} = Dockd.up(name, opts)

    # Rewrite the package with a different env -> drift.
    write_package(root, name, @image, env: ["A=2"])

    assert {:ok, %{action: :recreated, instance: recreated}} = Dockd.up(name, opts)
    refute recreated.id === inst.id
    assert "A=2" in recreated.env
  end

  test "errors when the package is absent and no --source is given", %{opts: opts} do
    assert {:error, %Dockd.Error{phase: :validate, message: message}} =
             Dockd.up("does-not-exist", opts)

    assert message =~ "not installed"
  end

  defp write_package(root, name, image, spec_fields) do
    dir = Path.join(root, name)
    File.mkdir_p!(dir)
    body = Enum.into(spec_fields, %{"name" => name, "image" => image})
    File.write!(Path.join(dir, "package.json"), Jason.encode!(body))
  end

  defp unique_name, do: "up-test-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
end

printf '{"name":"smoke","image":"busybox:1.37.0","shell":"/bin/sh"}' > "$ROOT/smoke/package.json"
export DOCKD_PACKAGES_PATH="$ROOT"
echo "=== up (create) ==="; mix dockd instance up --package smoke 2>&1 | grep -v "\[info\]"
echo "=== up again (idempotent) ==="; mix dockd instance up --package smoke 2>&1 | grep -v "\[info\]"
echo "=== up --json ==="; mix dockd instance up --package smoke --json 2>&1 | grep -v "\[info\]"
echo "=== missing package, no source ==="; mix dockd instance up --package nope 2>&1 | grep -v "\[info\]"
mix dockd instance destroy --name smoke 2>&1 | grep -v "\[info\]" >/dev/null
